mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPI YoY > 2%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a weakening labor market, which is typically associated with a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which negatively impacts corporate revenues and thus S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where RSAFS declines for 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals supply chain disruptions or a contraction in manufacturing, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO declines > 1%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy, which typically boosts equity markets, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal where a decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in a month during a late-cycle expansion signals a weakening demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where HOUST declines > 5% during late-cycle expansion, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a combination of a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a broad economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO declines and UNRATE rises, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
